instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle.

Trim any fat off the 1.5 lb pork tenderloin. To take off the thin, shiny silver skin, slide a thin knife under one end of it and cut along the length, angling the blade up toward the skin. Pat the pork dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, stir together the 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp coriander.
Rub 1 tbsp of the olive oil all over the pork. Sprinkle the spice mix over it and rub it in with your hands until it's coated on every side.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large oven safe skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Lay in the pork and brown it on all sides, turning it every 1 to 2 minutes, about 6 minutes in all. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.

Put the skillet in the oven and roast for 7 minutes. Flip the pork over and roast it for another 6 to 8 minutes. You're cooking it to 145°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when the middle is faintly pink and the juices run clear.
Use an oven mitt to take out the skillet, and lay a dry towel over the handle. It stays very hot. Move the pork to a cutting board, cover it loosely with foil and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Set the skillet over medium heat and pour in the 1/2 cup chicken broth. It'll hiss. Scrape up the brown bits from the bottom and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's cooked down by about half.
Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the 1 tbsp cold butter until it melts into the sauce. Pour in any juices from the cutting board. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Slice the pork into 1/2 inch rounds. If you're keeping some for lunches, set those slices aside before you sauce the rest.
Serve the slices with the pan sauce spooned over them.
method_notes: All three sear the tenderloin in an oven safe skillet and finish it in a 390 to 400°F oven, then rest it before slicing. Natasha's Kitchen (the most rated) rubs it with oil and a dry mix of salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and coriander, browns it for 6 minutes and roasts it for 13 to 15 minutes, flipping halfway, to about 150°F. Well Plated uses a paprika, brown sugar and cumin rub, pulls it at 135°F and spoons the pan juices over the slices; RecipeTin Eats seasons it with salt and pepper only and builds a creamy marsala sauce in the same skillet. This one follows Natasha's rub and timing, cooks to 145°F, and makes a small broth and butter pan sauce in the skillet.
